Definition: Does the government maintain a digital land register?
Comments: Digital land registry (LIFE electronic book consultation); Doing Business notes digitization.
revision_notes: Both original sources were fetched and remain live/relevant: econsultation.dgi.gouv.ci is confirmed as the electronic Livre Foncier (land register) consultation portal, and the Doing Business 2020 profile covers registering property but is now dated. Fresh searches confirm the land register has developed considerably since 2020 via SIGFU (Systeme Integre de Gestion du Foncier Urbain, Decree 2021-862), which digitises urban land records with electronic signature (SIGNE) since January 2024 and a unique parcel identifier (IDUFCI). However coverage remains geographically partial (initially Greater Abidjan and Assinie, expanding) and the separate rural land system (SIFOR-CI, created by Ordonnance 2025-85 of 12 February 2025) only issued its first electronic land certificates in March 2026, in a single region (Moronou). This confirms the register is digitally operational but not yet fully deployed nationwide, consistent with the original score of 4 (Partially deployed). Score confirmed unchanged; sources and year updated to reflect current evidence.
revised_comments: The government maintains a digital land register via the Systeme Integre de Gestion du Foncier Urbain (SIGFU), established by Decree No. 2021-862, which centralises urban land applications, parcel history and cadastral data under a unique parcel identifier (IDUFCI) and has used electronic signature (SIGNE) for land title deeds since January 2024. The electronic Livre Foncier can be consulted online via the tax authority's e-consultation portal. Coverage began with Greater Abidjan and Assinie and is expanding progressively. A separate rural land digitisation system, SIFOR-CI, was established in February 2025 under the Agence Fonciere Rurale, with the first electronic rural land certificates issued in March 2026 in the Moronou region, indicating that rural deployment is still at an early stage. Overall, the land register is digitally operational and actively expanding but not yet deployed nationwide.
